conventions.convention: Affine class scores use finite ordered labels 1 through K; ties select the smallest maximizing label.
Indicator-response fitting selects the least-squares minimizer of smallest Frobenius norm, allows rank-deficient designs, and includes an intercept only when supplied as a design column.
Gaussian generative models assume AC, strictly positive class priors, and symmetric positive-definite covariance matrices; LDA shares one covariance.
Binary logistic labels are 0 and 1; a zero logit predicts 0. Softmax labels are 1 through K with smallest-index ties. Neither conditional model assumes Gaussian features.

The likelihood uses a nonempty finite fixed design and conditionally independent binary responses. With an intercept, its coefficient is unpenalized; without an intercept, every coefficient receives the L1 penalty. No optimizer existence is asserted.
The perceptron augments inputs as (x,1), starts at zero, visits the fixed sample order, updates on signed margin ≤ 0, predicts −1 at a score tie, and stops only after a complete pass without updates.
The logistic Newton/IRLS identities concern one unpenalized update at finite coefficients; inverse formulas require full column rank and assert no iterative convergence.

load_bearing.statement: The sigmoid is σ(t)=(1+e^(−t))^(−1). Binary logistic conditional probabilities use finite affine logits, with label 0 at a zero logit; softmax probabilities normalize exponentials of finite affine class logits.

For the specified finite fixed design and conditionally independent responses, ℓ(β)=Σ_i[y_i x_iᵀβ−log(1+exp(x_iᵀβ))]. The L1 objective leaves a reserved intercept unpenalized and otherwise penalizes all coefficients; no optimizer existence is asserted.

Starting at w=0 with augmented inputs (x_i,1), visit the nonempty finite ordered sample repeatedly, update w by y_i(x_i,1) whenever the signed margin is nonpositive, and return w after a full pass without updates; otherwise continue.

Under AC, positive priors and positive-definite Gaussian covariances, the defined log posterior differs by a class-independent term from the displayed affine LDA score under common covariance, or the displayed quadratic QDA score with class-specific covariances. Ties select the smallest class index.
For a nonempty finite binary logistic sample, if a vector v satisfies (2y_i−1)x_iᵀv>0 for every i, then sup over finite β of ℓ(β) is zero and no finite coefficient vector attains it.

Among all minimizers of the indicator-response squared Frobenius residual there is a unique minimum-Frobenius-norm coefficient matrix. It is V_r D_r^(−1) U_rᵀY for positive rank, and zero for rank zero; all minimizers are B_*+N with XN=0.

published_dependencies.used_for: Existence, normal equations and kernel description of ordinary and weighted finite-dimensional least-squares minimizers.
Thin SVD, row/kernel orthogonality and the rank-zero branch of the minimum-norm indicator fit.
Explicit inherited choice assumption in the Gaussian model, score theorem and shared-boundary example.
Meaning and existence of the Gaussian conditional laws, with their AC qualification.
Positive-definite Gaussian density used to derive LDA and QDA posterior scores.
Convexity of the smooth negative logistic log-likelihood on the open convex domain R^q.
Finite Bernoulli response-family support, normalization, moments and local derivative-envelope requirements.
Canonical Bernoulli-logit GLM and common scale a=1.
Specialization of score, expected information and positive weights to Bernoulli logistic regression.
Working response, positive weights and weighted least-squares convention for one IRLS update.
Identification of the full-rank Bernoulli IRLS update with Fisher scoring after verifying the supplier's regularity hypotheses.
Comparison of separator progress with weight norm in the perceptron update bound.

concerns.concern: The title says “repeat a two-pass cycle”, whereas the Example and Verification show w=0 → (0,1) → 0 within every single pass. The repeated cycle consists of two updates in one pass; the title misdescribes its period.

Verification 2.1 says “Every finite coefficient has likelihood strictly below zero by [F2]”. The cited theorem and calculation concern log-likelihood. The likelihood itself is positive, with unattained supremum one; “likelihood” here should read “log-likelihood”.

seams_checked.note: The consumer page declares this prerequisite. Its def-bradley-terry-preference-model declares the logistic-model dependency and cites precisely the same finite-real sigmoid σ(t)=(1+e^(−t))^(−1). Finite real reward differences satisfy that interface; reversing a comparison uses σ(−t)=1−σ(t). The supplier imposes no Gaussian feature law, independence across comparisons, or deterministic preference interpretation, and the consumer imports none of those.
